overview.text: Frequency describes how often a repeating event occurs: it is the number of cycles or oscillations completed—or waves passing a fixed point—per unit time. It is a core way to characterize periodic motion and waves, alongside period, amplitude, and (for waves) wavelength. If one cycle takes period T, frequency f = 1/T, so a faster repetition has a shorter period. Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz), with 1 Hz equal to one cycle per second. For a traveling wave, speed v equals frequency times wavelength (v = fλ); when wave speed in a medium is fixed, higher frequency corresponds to shorter wavelength. In sound, higher frequency is heard as higher pitch.

key_facts.text: For repeating motion, the period is the time taken for one complete oscillation; frequency counts oscillations per unit time.
Frequency and period are reciprocals: f = 1/T. A shorter period means a higher frequency.
The hertz (Hz) is the SI unit of frequency; 1 Hz equals one cycle per second.
For a traveling wave, v = fλ; at a fixed wave speed, increasing frequency means decreasing wavelength.
For sound, higher frequency corresponds to higher pitch.
